messages:
Priya (customer): Hey team, after our Okta OIDC config change this morning multiple devs hit 403 in the Redwood console when opening Projects -> Settings. Worked yesterday.
Maya S (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error you see and the repro steps? Any chance it's just a browser cache?
Priya (customer): Repro steps: login via SSO -> click org -> select project -> Settings -> receive a page that says "403 permission denied". Screenshot attached in thread. Happens in incognito too.
Maya S (support): Got it. Which claim are you mapping groups from in Okta? groups, group_names, or a custom claim?
Priya (customer): We recently flipped to emit a custom claim called "okta_groups" (previously it was "groups"). Our SCIM sync is still on but we moved to claims-only mapping for speed.
Jonah K (identity): That rings alarm bells — our role mapping currently looks at "groups" and "group_names" claims. If Okta started emitting "okta_groups" only, the mapping could drop all roles.
Maya S (support): Can you grab the id token payload when you log in and paste the groups claim? You can run: 
```
console.log(jwt_decode(id_token))
```
or paste the decoded payload here.
Priya (customer): Pasted payload (redacted): 
```
{
  "sub": "00u1234...",
  "email": "priya@acme.co",
  "okta_groups": ["acme-admins","acme-developers"]
}
```
Maya S (support): Okay — that confirms it. Our mapping didn't see "okta_groups" so user got no roles. That yields 403 on project settings.
Sarah L (acct): Is this something we can hotfix client-side or do customers need to change Okta to emit "groups" again?
Jonah K (identity): We can push a quick change to accept alternate group claim names as a fallback (okta_groups, groupnames, memberOf). But need to be careful for collisions. Short-term workaround: assign Priya an org-level role manually so she can proceed.
Maya S (support): Priya — can you confirm the email used to log in? I can grant a temporary org admin role for 1 hour while we fix mapping.
Priya (customer): It's priya@acme.co. Appreciate the temporary access.
Maya S (support): Granting temp role now...
deploy-bot: deploy started: idp/claim-fallback-patch -> staging (build 2026.3.11)
Maya S (support): Done — I pushed a one-hour org.admin grant to priya@acme.co. Can you try Settings again?
Priya (customer): Trying... yes, I can access Settings now. Thank you!! :partying_face:
Jonah K (identity): I'm going to roll the claim-fallback to prod after validation. It will map okta_groups -> groups when groups are absent. Patch notes: 
- fallback for claims: okta_groups, groupnames, memberOf
- telemetry to flag any customers relying on non-standard claims
Maya S (support): ETA for prod deploy?
deploy-bot: deployed idp/claim-fallback-patch -> production (build 2026.3.12) at 2026-03-10T16:12:34Z
Jonah K (identity): Prod is live. Priya, once you re-login the mapping should pick up your groups and your temporary grant will expire.
Priya (customer): Re-logged in, still in, I see my roles restored and Settings access persists. Looks good.
Sarah L (acct): I'll follow up with acme's SSO admin to suggest emitting the standard "groups" claim or keep the fallback in mind. Also logging this as a known issue in the onboarding docs.
Maya S (support): Closing the thread once we confirm no other users affected. Priya, please reopen if anyone else at your org hits similar 403s.
Priya (customer): Will do. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround! :heart:
